title: Truck advertising jobs and band battles on corners
summary: Playing short numbers from a truck and meeting rival bands at corners.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: How was that kind of work, working on the truck Alba? Would that be harder than playing a dance or what would you say that kind of work would be?
No it wasn't harder than playing a dance because on the truck you'd just run, you'd just play about every second corner you'd play a short number. Just to draw the people's attention.
You'd usually play like a jump number or?
Yeah. Sometimes you'd play blues. Just mix them in you know.
Did you ever run into any other bands that way on the corners too?
Oh yeah, you'd run into a lot of bands. In those days yeah, meet up on the corners alongside each other. Made the best man win.
But you'd still keep playing short numbers. Oh yeah. About, what did you say, about two or four choruses?
About three or four choruses, yeah. Did you ever play with Chris? Everybody would pick their best numbers for advertising. Pick four or five numbers and just play that all the while they advertise.
